A plain endpoint diff of that range therefore drags in those 3 out-of-scope commits' files (infra/aws/ec2/canonical-schwab-si2/*.ps1, org/tier2_senior/0.8.0_AE_CloudComp/*). To honor the explicit scope ("Two commits… IGNORE all other working-tree changes… Files center on data/inf/scripts/gold/"), the diff is path-restricted to `-- data/inf/scripts/gold/`. This is exact and lossless: every file touched by C1 (7 files) and C2 (16 files) lives under that path, and none of the 3 intervening commits touch it (they touch only infra/ and org/), so the path-scoped endpoint diff == the union of the two round-8 commits. Confirmed non-empty (141.7 KB, 20 unique files, +1541/-808 lines under the path).

WHAT CHANGED: This is round-8 of the INF advisor-of-record (AoR) attribution refactor (LD-0277, Andrew's SSOT design), replacing round-7's false-greening drift monitor with a single-source-of-truth resolver. C1 introduces the front-of-chain resolver (new INF_A_0.aor_resolver.py + new lib/aor_resolution.py providing load_resolution/apply_resolution_fold and the canonical aor_resolution.parquet + an APPEND event ledger at gold/dimensions/aor_ledger/events/{run-ts}.parquet — a new timestamped key every run so it is uncollapsible by construction), rewrites the detector in lib/aor_attribution_audit.py to ledger-diff CHANGES-only and DROP the as-of freshness gate, retires INF_A_01's comparison-emit path, and adds/rewrites tests (new test_aor_resolution.py, heavily rewritten test_aor_attribution_audit.py). C2 is the 14-site consumer migration: all AoR-consuming views inherit the canonical resolution instead of deriving locally — fold census collapses 10->1 (apply_advisor_of_record_fold now only in the resolver) via full-attach (A_00/A_01) or movers-only apply_resolution_fold (INF_09/B_00/C_01/D_00c/D_00d/D_00f/D_02b), and household resolution collapses 4->1 in C_07 with C_02/D_02c/D_00d/D_04 inheriting via household_headline_map; inflection_rep_scope.py and orion-gold-dispatch.sh are updated accordingly. The AOR_FOLD_ACTIVE switch is OFF and files carry DEPLOY-SERVE-HELD markers; the whole migration is intended to be DELTA-0 under OFF (pure structural refactor), with go-live being a single switch-flip.

CLAUDE.md: Only the repo-root CLAUDE.md applies (no user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md; no CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md in data/, data/inf/, data/inf/scripts/, or data/inf/scripts/gold/).

(Rule 14) every .py edit passes .tools/commit-gate.sh (py_compile + ds-precommit-check AST/silver-ids + ruff py39 pin 0.15.11). (Code Quality) NO emojis / non-ASCII in production code, logs, or anything running on AWS — use OK:/WARN:/ERROR:/SKIP:/BLOCKED: (breaks CloudWatch/charmap/CI). (NEVER #4) never trigger ad-hoc gold runs to validate — validate on the scheduled nightly's artifacts. (NEVER #2 / blocker W) never move served output without never-widen CTO+COO sign-off; a verified DELTA=0 deploy needs no hold — directly relevant to the DELTA-0-under-OFF go-live gate. (NEVER #5 / Rule 22a) never trust a producer's self-report or rc=0 — ground behavioral/served claims by exercising the path and reading the SERVED artifact, not source; ground causal 'why' claims in source+graph (file:line @ commit). (Rule 20) check the dependency graph before changing a gold script — comp-pipescript io [script] for column gaps + portal consumers, comp-blast [fn] for blast radius. SOVEREIGN-hold context: the 49F/Schwab/black_diamond prohibition does NOT cover this work — INF (inf/mdpf) is explicitly IN SCOPE per the standing prohibition memo, so this pipeline is reviewable.

If INF_D_11 fails to run for more than 2 consecutive nights, a real per-account attribution change whose event file now predates the window is dropped from in_window and never alerted -- the human is never told of the served attribution swap (a monitor-of-the-monitor gap).

The portal keeps showing advisor-of-record attribution AFTER the rollback meant to undo it -- a silent served DELTA that the switch-off was supposed to revert. (And if the resolution artifact is ever absent while the switch is 0 with consumer code deployed, every AoR consumer RAISEs and the whole INF nightly aborts.) The file's own comment says the entry must be made unconditional at GO, but the committed code does not implement it, contradicting the 'single switch-flip go-live / switch-only rollback reverts to servicing' contract.

result.summary: This xhigh-effort review covers the INF round-8 advisor-of-record (AoR) refactor, which moves AoR into a single SSOT resolver (INF_A_0 / aor_resolution.py) that ~10 gold consumers now inherit from. The load-bearing correctness findings cluster into four root causes: (A) the resolver stays switch-gated in dispatch while consumers call load_resolution() unconditionally, so the documented switch-only rollback either silently persists the fold or hard-aborts the nightly, and DELTA-0-under-OFF is unreachable; (C) the servicing-key basis silently flips from rep_name-slug to rep_id-primary, making DELTA-0-under-OFF (blocker W) empirical rather than structural; (B) household_headline_map now RAISES where the retired resolve_household_advisor degraded gracefully, giving household consumers new hard-abort paths; and (D) attach_advisor_key ships NaN advisor_key on any A_00-vs-resolver partition/as-of skew. The remainder are detector-completeness regressions (deleted coverage-drop detection, unparseable-key masking, cache-trust false-green, lookback aging), a resolver-write blast-radius issue, a name-allowlist SSOT test gap, and load_resolution-in-loop plus duplication/diagnostic cleanups.
